purpose: Six Monogram Coffee Takesi coffees transcribed from a user-provided Urlicht Coffee product image. This set is a local candidate record for profile-based recommendation only: it contains no tasting outcome labels and must not be used to fit, tune, or test the personal profile.

source_policy.descriptor_status: Seller claims transcribed from the supplied image, not verified cup perceptions.
source_policy.description_status: Product facts and promotional copy are image-derived unless a research source is named explicitly.
source_policy.scoring_boundary: Seller descriptions, farm reputation, accolades, variety prestige, price, package size, and peaberry sorting do not affect personal fit unless represented by an existing explicitly scored field.

recommendation_snapshot.evidence_base: 51 rated observations: Loved 7, Liked 34, Ok 10, Disliked 0.
recommendation_snapshot.score_note: Fit and novelty are deterministic ordering signals, not probabilities. Direct-history adjustment is unavailable in this portable score. Estate reputation, accolades, price, variety prestige, package size, and peaberry sorting are excluded from both scores.

farm_research.summary: A high-altitude specialty estate founded in 2001 in Yanacachi, Sud Yungas, La Paz, Bolivia. Its strongest objective evidence is first place with 93.36 points in the 2009 Bolivia Cup of Excellence. The farm says it maintains relationships with five demanding international micro-roasters, including Monogram Coffee.
farm_research.altitude_note: The seller image prints 1940-2600 masl for all six coffees. Takesi's current site describes its lots as 1850-2300 masl, while Coffee Collective describes the broader farm valley as 1700-2600 masl. Keep 1940-2600 as seller-declared metadata, not a verified exact-lot altitude.

sources.title: Bolivia 2009 - Cup of Excellence
sources.evidence: Agrotakesi SA placed first with 93.36 points.

sources.title: Takesi - Nosotros
sources.evidence: Farm history, Yanacachi location, high-altitude lots, and named long-term roaster relationships.

sources.title: Takesi - Coffee Collective
sources.evidence: High-altitude growing context, quality-control organization, and predominantly washed processing.

sources.title: Exclusive Micro-Release - Takesi Java, Bolivia
sources.evidence: Java production history and an experienced roaster's lot-level assessment; promotional and contextual, not a personal fit signal.

sources.title: World Coffee Research - Java
sources.evidence: Java lineage, agronomic traits, and quality potential.

sources.title: World Coffee Research - SL28
sources.evidence: SL28 lineage, agronomic traits, and established variety reputation.
